newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-SPARTA PRAGUE CLINCHES 3RD TITLE IN FOUR YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTA PRAGUE CLINCHES 3RD TITLE IN FOUR YEARS.

text.p: Sparta Prague, after a slow start in the Czech first division, clinched their third title in four years on Sunday when a 2-1 win over Sigma Olomouc put them four points clear of crosstown rival Slavia Prague with only one game left.
Sparta were tied for fourth place after the autumn season but won 12 of their next 14 games to overtake Slavia, who lost a crucial match on Sunday 1-0 to third place Jablonec.
"It was terrible. The noise the crowd made when they learned Slavia lost, and we were trailing (1-0). But I knew we could win, I kept believing," said Sparta keeper Michal Caloun.

Just as they had in the standings, Sparta fought back in the second half with an equaliser by striker Vratislav Lokvenc in the 59th minute. Scoring leader Horst Siegl then gave Sparta the title with a gaol in the 90th minute, his 20th of the season.
The win gives Sparta their 23rd title overall, 20 of which came in the former Czechoslovakia, which split into separate Czech and Slovak states in 1993.

The title also salvages some pride -- and ensures a spot in European Cup play next year -- for Sparta, who bowed out of the Czech-Moravian Cup in the quarter-finals with an unexpected extra-time loss to Banik Ostrava.
